annotations.title: Compare your page with the cited answer

description:
Compare your own page's structure against the AI-generated answer
actually cited for this keyword, and return a fix brief: the differences
between the two, each with the change worth testing, not just a
description of the winner. Use this to answer 'how does my page differ
from what AI cites for this, and what could I try'. The brief lists
things to test, not proven causes of citation. It never contains the
cited answer's text.

Read-only: no side effects, safe to retry. Costs 1 quota unit per sample
(1 by default; free tier is 30 units/month shared across every metered
tool, so up to 30 single-sample calls to this tool alone if nothing else
is used that period). A sample that fails is not charged.

Returns: {"keyword", "your_url", "already_cited" (bool: your page's site
is among the answer's sources, in at least half of them with samples
above 1; when true, fix_brief is one line saying so instead of changes),
"basis" (one sentence: how many answers, which engine and market, and
that the brief lists things to test), "samples_ok" and
"cited_in_answers" (only with samples above 1), "winning" (structure of the
AI-cited answer, same shape as analyze_citation_structure), "yours"
(same structure computed for your_url, including its own "outline" and
"has_table", with "num_links_out"/"linked_domains" standing in for
source count), "gaps" (list of plain-English differences worth acting
on), "possibly_missing" (heads from the winning outline whose key words
mostly do not appear on your page; word matching, so check each before
adding it), "fix_brief" (list, most important first, each line what was
observed then what is worth testing: opening, number, list, sections,
missing points, table, then a reminder to write in your own words - or a
"no structural change indicated" line when every check already matches -
and always last, one off-site option drawn from the winning answer's
source_mix: which community sites (Reddit, YouTube, X...) it cites, or
which other sites to get mentioned on). With samples above 1, "winning"
is the first answer, and a brief line or missing point needs at least half
the answers behind it}, or {"error"} if either side couldn't be
fetched/parsed.

Args:
    keyword: the topic/query to check, e.g. "best project management tool".
    your_url: full URL of your own page to compare, e.g.
        "https://example.com/best-project-management-tools".
    country: market to read the cited answer in, e.g. "Italy". Defaults
        to "United States".
    language: language code, e.g. "it". Defaults to "en".
    engine: "chat_gpt" (default), "gemini" or "perplexity": whose answer
        to compare your page against.
    samples: how many independent answers to read, 1 to 5. Default 1.
        Answers change from run to run; 3 gives a steadier brief.
name: analyze_citation_gap
title: Compare your page with the cited answer
